sentences.zh: 当时总共价值60万美元。

sentences.en: Congratulations, you won the lottery.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们谈论的是微不足道的钱。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 但这又是那种疯狂的游戏设计，需要花费数周或数月才能真正，你知道的，进行一次抽奖以筹集足够的资金。

sentences.en: Which all of $600,000 at the time.
sentences.zh: 他们做了一些现场赛马，比如抽奖活动。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're talking about pennies.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，它不管用。

sentences.en: But this is, again, this insane game design that takes many weeks or months to actually, you know, have a drawing to get enough money.
sentences.zh: 而且确实是从1970年新泽西州彩票开业并增加每周一次的游戏开始，各州才终于摸透了门道。

sentences.en: They do some live horse racing, like sweepstakes.
sentences.zh: 1970年开业的新泽西州彩票，他们真正找到了这些早期彩票如何运作的中奖秘诀。

sentences.en: But as you said, it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 与那些需要数周或数月抽奖的昂贵彩票不同，他们为每周一次、奖金5万美元的游戏提供50美分的彩票。

sentences.en: And it's really only starting in 1970 when the New Jersey lottery starts up and adds a weekly game that the states finally figure it out.
sentences.zh: 对于当时来说，这是相当大笔的头奖，并且开奖速度非常非常快。

sentences.en: The New Jersey lottery, which starts in 1970, they really hit on the winning formula for how these early lotteries are going to operate.
sentences.zh: 这将吸引更多的人来玩。

sentences.en: And rather than these expensive tickets with drawings that take weeks or months, they offer 50-cent tickets for weekly games with $50,000 drawings.
sentences.zh: 廉价的彩票，平易近人的彩票，随处售卖。

sentences.en: So pretty good-sized jackpots for the time that move really, really quickly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，纽约彩票刚开张时，他们试图在银行里卖彩票，因为他们认为这样安全。

sentences.en: And that will entice a lot more people to play.
sentences.zh: 然后国会就说，没门儿。

sentences.en: Cheap tickets, accessible tickets, sold everywhere.
sentences.zh: 就像，你不能这么做。

sentences.en: You know, the New York lottery, when they start up, they try to sell the tickets in banks because they think it will be secure.
sentences.zh: 你不能在银行里卖彩票。

sentences.en: And then Congress is like, no f***ing way.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like, you can't do that.
sentences.zh: 就像，这完全违背了银行本应代表的储蓄伦理。

sentences.en: You can't sell lottery tickets in banks.
sentences.zh: 所以，但在新泽西州，就像，它在酒类商店、酒吧和理发店里卖，对吧？

sentences.en: That's insane.
sentences.zh: 就像，真的，它们更接近我们今天已经熟悉的现代州立彩票销售伦理和精神。

sentences.en: Like, it's the exact opposite of the sort of ethic of savings that banks are supposed to be about.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了一点让我觉得非常有趣的事情，那就是在游戏的设计中，频率真的很重要。

sentences.en: So, but in New Jersey, like, it's selling them in liquor stores and in bars and in barbershops, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，或者是即时性。

sentences.en: Like, really, they get closer to the modern state lottery sales ethic and ethos that we've come to be familiar with today.
sentences.zh: 就像，你买了一张彩票，你希望它，你知道的，在那天或者，你知道的，就快要兑现。

sentences.en: So you hit on something that I find really interesting is that inside of the sort of the design of the game, frequency is really important.
sentences.zh: 而这是这些事情能够腾飞的唯一真正途径。

sentences.en: Like, or immediacy.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Like, you buy a ticket, you want it to, like, pay out, you know, that day or, you know, like, really soon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真正的例子就是刮刮乐彩票，对吧，

sentences.en: And that's the only real way for these things to take off.
sentences.zh: 它于1974年在马萨诸塞州首次推出，然后像野火一样在各彩票州蔓延开来，最后甚至非常非常快地蔓延到非彩票州，

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 因为它们提供的那种即时性。

sentences.en: And that's, I mean, the real example of this is scratch tickets, right,
sentences.zh: 我真的对州立彩票像接触性病毒一样蔓延的方式着迷。

sentences.en: which were introduced for the first time in Massachusetts in 1974 and then just spread like wildfire across lottery states and then eventually even to non-lottery states very,
sentences.zh: 就像，如果你隔壁的州有彩票而你的州没有彩票，你很快就会有彩票了。

sentences.en: very quickly because of that immediacy that they offer.
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下那里发生了什么，以及那种心理学以及它是如何感染州议会的吗？

sentences.en: I'm truly fascinated by the way that state lotteries spread like a contact virus.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, if the state next to you has a lottery and your state doesn't have a lottery, you are going to get the lottery very soon.
sentences.zh: 州立彩票在第一波浪潮中的蔓延，也就是从1963年到1977年，与我们今天看到的与大麻合法化的情况有许多相似之处，

sentences.en: Can you describe what is going on there and the sort of psychology of that and how it infects state legislatures?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 州立彩票在第一波浪潮中的蔓延，也就是从1963年到1977年，与我们今天看到的与大麻合法化的情况有许多相似之处，

sentences.en: There are a lot of parallels between the spread of state lotteries in this first wave, so from 1963 to 1977, and what we're seeing today with marijuana legalization,
sentences.zh: 而我们今天看到的...

sentences.en: with sports betting, lots of other state policies work this way,
sentences.zh: 在体育博彩方面，许多其他的州政策也是这样运作的

sentences.en: which is that once a neighboring state legalizes something, anything,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，一旦某个邻近的州将某种东西合法化，任何东西

sentences.en: and invariably people who live outside that state are going to come over and play your lottery or play your sports betting or buy your weed.
sentences.zh: 住在该州以外的人肯定会跑过来玩你们的彩票、玩你们的体育博彩或者买你们的大麻

sentences.en: Of course, what happens in practice is that by more states legalizing, it just spreads it further, as you said, like a contact virus.
sentences.zh: 当然，实际情况是，随着越来越多的州将其合法化，就像你说的，它就像接触性病毒一样进一步扩散

sentences.en: So, this logic, and I'm going to keep coming back to this because this is, I think, the key point here,
sentences.zh: 所以，这个逻辑——我还会不断回到这一点，因为我认为这是这里的关键点

sentences.en: this belief that gambling is inevitable sort of keeps the spread going and going and keeps adding new games and keeps adding new states, but it's not inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这种认为赌博不可避免的信念，使得这种扩散没完没了，不断增加新的游戏，不断增加新的州，但它并不是不可避免的

sentences.en: It's inevitable because states make it so by assuming that it is inevitable in the first place.
sentences.zh: 之所以不可避免，是因为州政府首先做出了它不可避免的假设

sentences.en: Another thing you talk about in your book is that these august bodies take great pains to justify the lottery and sort of square it with their morals,
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到的另一件事是，这些德高望重的机构煞费苦心地为彩票辩护，并试图让它符合他们的道德观念

sentences.en: and one of the ways they do this is by saying, well, if we have a legalized form of this, we can sort of suppress the mafia version of the lottery or the numbers version,
sentences.zh: 他们的方法之一就是说，好吧，如果我们有这种玩法的合法形式，我们就可以某种程度上压制黑帮版本的彩票或地下数字彩

sentences.en: all the illegal versions of this.
sentences.zh: 所有这些非法版本

sentences.en: Can you talk about how the lottery is sold to the public as an effective way to suppress vice and even could be virtuous because buying a lottery ticket then fills the state's coffers so it can buy good things and fund wholesome programs?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈彩票是如何向公众兜售的吗？说它是压制恶习的有效方法，甚至可以说是美德，因为买彩票能充实国库，从而购买好东西并资助健康的计划

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对

sentences.en: So, this is like the lesson that people take away from prohibition is that there's no point in trying to suppress something that people are trying to do anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是人们从禁酒令中吸取的教训，即试图压制人们无论如何都要去做的事情是没有意义的

sentences.en: I mean the prohibition of alcohol.
sentences.zh: 我是指禁酒令

sentences.en: This is happening anyway, illegally.
sentences.zh: 这无论如何都在发生，以非法的形式

sentences.en: It is draining money from our police resources and our state resources.
sentences.zh: 它正在消耗我们警察资源和国家资源的资金

sentences.en: The state might as well legalize it to make money, and as you said, we could even make it a civic good.
sentences.zh: 国家索性把它合法化来赚钱，正如你所说，我们甚至可以把它变成一项公民福利

sentences.en: We can fund our government.
sentences.zh: 我们可以资助我们的政府

sentences.en: We'll never have to pay taxes again because we'll have all this money that is being raised by illegal games.
sentences.zh: 我们再也不用交税了，因为我们将拥有通过非法游戏筹集的所有这些资金

sentences.en: So, that's the other crazy point is all these investigations into illegal gambling, all they do is just give people the impression that gambling is really, really lucrative
sentences.zh: 所以，另一个疯狂的点是，所有这些对非法赌博的调查，它们所做的只是给人们留下一种印象，即赌博真的非常赚钱

sentences.en: and have this ironic consequence of incentivizing states to just legalize it because they think it's going to be super profitable rather than turn people off from gambling.
sentences.zh: 并产生了一个讽刺的后果，那就是激励各州将其合法化，因为它们认为这会超级赚钱，而不是让人对赌博产生反感

sentences.en: Like, imagine every time there was a drug bust, people are like, oh, man, we should legalize heroin.
sentences.zh: 就像，想象一下每次打击毒品犯罪时，人们都会说，天哪，我们应该把海洛因合法化

sentences.en: Look at how much money all the drug dealers are making.
sentences.zh: 看看所有毒贩赚了多少钱

sentences.en: You know, but it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但这并没有发生

sentences.en: But that's like the equivalent of what happened with lotteries in the 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是60和70年代彩票事件的翻版

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对

sentences.en: And so, describe that.
sentences.zh: 那么，请描述一下这一点

sentences.en: When state-sponsored lotteries are first being sort of proposed as a solution to the state's financial woes, what are people saying?
sentences.zh: 当由州赞助的彩票最初作为解决州财政困境的方案被提出时，人们都在说些什么？

sentences.en: And then what is the sort of result of it?
sentences.zh: 然后结果又是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: Like, their estimations for what they're going to get out of this are, you know, really outsized and, like, through the roof.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们对能从中获得多少收益的估计，你知道，真的是大得离谱，简直突破天际

sentences.en: And then in the end, like, why is it that they're not paying out the way that they think they are?
sentences.zh: 然后到头来，为什么它们没有像他们想象的那样带来回报呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错

sentences.en: So, this is what I think takes it from just regular politicians sort of overselling the thing that they're doing to why it's irrational, stupid, hopeful,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这正是将普通政客夸大推销他们正在做的事情，升华到了为什么它是不理性的、愚蠢的、充满希望的

sentences.en: wishful in the way that gamblers behave.
sentences.zh: 就像赌徒行为中的一厢情愿

sentences.en: In the 1960s and 70s, there's this belief, you know, and I'm not exaggerating, this belief that a lottery is going to singularly solve states' financial probleMs.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60和70年代，有一种信念，你知道，我没有夸大其词，这种信念认为彩票将奇迹般地解决各州的财政问题

sentences.en: A New Jersey congressman says that we can increase every state service in New Jersey four times over if we make numbers games legal.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州的一名国会议员表示，如果我们把数字游戏合法化，我们可以把新泽西州每项公共服务的经费提高四倍

sentences.en: The belief that we'll never have to pay taxes ever again because we have a lottery.
sentences.zh: 这种信念认为，因为我们有了彩票，我们将再也不用交税了

sentences.en: And even this crazy cognitive dissonance, even after it doesn't work and the states have to raise taxes, this belief, hey, why are we raising taxes?
sentences.zh: 甚至还有这种疯狂的认知失调，即使在它不管用、各州不得不加税之后，这种信念依然存在：嘿，我们为什么要加税？

sentences.en: Didn't we have a lottery?
sentences.zh: 我们不是有彩票吗？

sentences.en: Shouldn't that have solved all of our financial problems?
sentences.zh: 难道那不应该解决我们所有的财务问题吗？

sentences.en: So, that's sort of the panacea, the first version of the panacea.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像万灵药，万灵药的第一版

sentences.en: And then you say, okay, it doesn't work in the Northeast and Rust Belt.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，好吧，它在东北部和铁锈带不管用

sentences.en: Surely these states sort of got wise and limited their expectations.
sentences.zh: 这些州肯定变聪明了，并限制了他们的期望

sentences.en: And they did, but in a whole new magic bullet-y kind of way where they now go in the 1980s not thinking that the lottery is going to solve all the problems for the entire state.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这样做了，但采用了一种全新的、带有“银弹”色彩的方式，他们在20世纪80年代不再认为彩票能解决整个州的所有问题

sentences.en: But, oh, it will surely solve all of our education problems or it will singularly fund public parks or police services.
sentences.zh: 而是，哦，它肯定能解决我们所有的教育问题，或者它将单独资助公园或警察服务

sentences.en: So, it's still a panacea, but we've just sort of limited ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以它仍然是万灵药，只是我们给自己设定了某种限制

sentences.en: And then that panacea doesn't work and there's still this cognitive dissonance.
sentences.zh: 然后这种万灵药也不起作用，并且仍然存在这种认知失调

sentences.en: And then in California, for example, which uses a lottery in 1984 to raise money for education,
sentences.zh: 然后以加利福尼亚州为例，该州在1984年利用彩票为教育筹集资金

sentences.en: there's this belief even afterwards that it's now hard to raise taxes for education because people think that the lottery is funding education and that we don't need any more money to pay for schools.
sentences.zh: 甚至在此之后，人们仍然有一种信念，即现在很难为教育提高税收，因为人们认为彩票正在资助教育，我们不再需要更多的钱来支付学校费用

sentences.en: And, of course, that doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并没有起作用

sentences.en: It's like 2% of the California education budget.
sentences.zh: 它大约只占加州教育预算的2%

sentences.en: But then come the 90s, still this cognitive dissonance, oh, if we have a lottery, it's like that arrested development line, like it fails for everybody else,
sentences.zh: 但到了90年代，依然存在这种认知失调，哦，如果我们有彩票——这就像那句《发展受阻》里的台词——尽管它在别人身上失败了

sentences.en: but surely it will work for us.
sentences.zh: 但它肯定会在我们身上起作用

sentences.en: Like, oh, it will still solve all of our problems, but we'll just reduce the problems a little bit more that they're going to solve.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，它仍然会解决我们所有的所有问题，但我们要解决的问题范围稍微缩减了一点点

sentences.en: Oh, in Georgia and other states in particular, it's we don't have enough students going to college, specifically in-state colleges and universities.
sentences.zh: 哦，在佐治亚州和其他一些州，具体情况是，我们没有足够的学生去上大学，特别是州内的学院和大学

sentences.en: So, we'll just use our lottery money to pay for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将只用彩票资金来支付这笔费用

sentences.en: So, that, okay, finally it works, first of all.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，首先它终于起作用了

sentences.en: Well, finally, the lottery actually sort of fulfills its mandate and does what they say it's going to do.
sentences.zh: 好吧，终于，彩票在某种程度上兑现了它的承诺，并做到了他们说它会做的事

sentences.en: But this belief over and over again, it's going to solve problem X and it doesn't solve problem X.
sentences.zh: 但这种信念一次又一次地出现：它将解决X问题，但它没有解决X问题

sentences.en: Oh, okay, but it will definitely solve problem Y.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，但它肯定会解决Y问题

sentences.en: Oh, it doesn't solve problem Y.
sentences.zh: 哦，它没有解决Y问题

sentences.en: Oh, it'll maybe solve this other problem instead.
sentences.zh: 哦，它也许会转而解决其他什么问题

sentences.en: They can't just say, hey, the lottery will be nice.
sentences.zh: 他们就是不能说，嘿，彩票挺不错的

sentences.en: It'll raise 2% of state revenue.
sentences.zh: 它将筹集到州收入的2%

sentences.en: You know, they can't do that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们做不到这一点

sentences.en: They have to sort of have this wing and a prayer that it's going to be a jackpot, you know, pun intended, for the state.
sentences.zh: 他们只能孤注一掷，盲目祈祷它能给国家带来头奖（双关语意）

sentences.en: Right, and 2% of state revenue isn't nearly enough to fund all the services that they're promising.
sentences.zh: 没错，州收入的2%远不足以资助他们承诺的所有服务

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣

sentences.en: So, could you describe what are the typical state lotto games and how they work and, you know, what customer base each of the games are appealing to?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能描述一下典型的州立彩票游戏是什么样的，它们是如何运作的，以及，你知道的，每种游戏吸引的是什么样的客户群吗？

sentences.en: If we're thinking about all 45 lottery states, because there are some games that are only played in some states, some games in others,
sentences.zh: 如果我们考虑到所有45个有彩票的州，因为有些游戏只在某些州玩，有些在其他州玩

sentences.en: there are really three big games that lotteries rely on.
sentences.zh: 彩票真正依赖的是三大游戏

sentences.en: The first and the one that needs to be mentioned first are scratch tickets, which account for as much as 60% to 65% of total annual lottery sales.
sentences.zh: 第一个也是首先需要提及的是刮刮乐，它占到全年彩票总销售额的60%到65%

sentences.en: And so, there are a couple different players for this.
sentences.zh: 所以，这类游戏有几种不同的玩家

sentences.en: What we've seen recently in scratch tickets is the, what I would call the sort of jackpotification of the games,
sentences.zh: 我们在最近的刮刮乐中看到的是，我称之为游戏“头奖化”的现象

sentences.en: where now you're buying scratch tickets that can cost as much as $100 in Texas.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你买的刮刮乐在德克萨斯州最高可以花到100美元

sentences.en: And we've gone from, they offered you a sort of distant chance at a big prize, but you're really playing for sort of the medium prize,
sentences.zh: 我们已经从过去那种提供获得大奖的渺茫机会，但你实际上是在为中等奖项而玩

sentences.en: to now there are scratch tickets that offer a $15 million jackpot.
sentences.zh: 演变成现在有提供1500万美元头奖的刮刮乐

sentences.en: Sort of meant to rival the lotto rollover Powerball Mega Millions type games.
sentences.zh: 这有点旨在与强力球（Powerball）和超级百万（Mega Millions）那种彩票滚存类游戏相媲美

sentences.en: What's cool about scratch tickets is the prize curve is shaped like a U, if you imagine, the letter U.
sentences.zh: 刮刮乐最酷的地方在于，如果你想象一下字母U，它的奖金曲线呈U字形

sentences.en: There are a lot of prizes concentrated at the very, very beginning.
sentences.zh: 有大量的奖金集中在非常、非常靠前的阶段

sentences.en: So, free tickets, $2 back, $5 back, and then there's a big gap, and then there's prizes at the very top, $20,000, $50,000, $100,000 more.
sentences.zh: 所以，免费彩票、返还2美元、返还5美元，然后有一个很大的断层，接着是顶端的奖金：2万美元、5万美元、10万美元甚至更多

sentences.en: On the assumption that no one's getting out of bed for $1,000.
sentences.zh: 基于这样的假设：没有人会为了1000美元而起早贪黑

sentences.zh: 并且基于这样的假设：如果你赢了5美元、10美元、20美元，你很可能会把钱再投进去买更多的彩票

sentences.en: So, you can play for your jackpot, and you can sort of keep playing, keep playing, keep playing, because you put $20 in, you get $10 back, you put $10 in, you get $7 back,
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以为了你的头奖而玩，并且你可以一直玩下去、玩下去、玩下去，因为你投了20美元进去，拿回了10美元，你投了10美元进去，拿回了7美元

sentences.zh: 你投了7美元进去，拿回了5美元，你知道的，诸如此类

sentences.zh: 突然之间，你在彩票上花掉了40美元，而你一开始甚至都没有40美元

sentences.en: That's sort of the bread and butter for lottery commissions.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是彩票委员会的摇钱树

sentences.en: As a result, sort of many types of players for those games, they are one of the most regressive lottery games, meaning the poor players play them more often,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于这些游戏有多种类型的玩家，它们是最具累退性的彩票游戏之一，这意味着较穷的玩家更经常玩它们

sentences.en: they spend a higher percentage of their money on them relative to other games.
sentences.zh: 相对于其他游戏而言，他们把更高比例的钱花在这些游戏上

sentences.en: The other sort of major regressive game, in particular, are numbers games, which we've already covered,
sentences.zh: 另一种主要的累退游戏，特别是数字游戏，我们之前已经讨论过了

sentences.en: which remain actually particularly and disproportionately popular among black gamblers.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这种游戏在黑人赌徒中仍然尤其且不成比例地受欢迎

sentences.en: And again, sort of have this historical roots in the black community that sort of carry them forward to today.
sentences.zh: 并且再次说明，它在黑人社区有着历史根源，并一直延续到今天

sentences.en: So, the state just in the mid-1970s just usurped these illegal games.
sentences.zh: 所以，州政府在20世纪70年代中期强占了这些非法游戏

sentences.en: And these are now, basically, they haven't changed the design.
sentences.zh: 而这些游戏现在基本上没有改变设计

sentences.en: The design that was created in 1924 by a black immigrant from the Dutch West Indies named Casper Holstein, they don't use, like, the newspaper anymore to pick the winning number,
sentences.zh: 由荷属安的列斯群岛的黑人移民卡斯珀·霍尔斯坦（Casper Holstein）于1924年创造的设计，他们虽然不再用报纸来挑选winning number（中奖号码）了

sentences.en: but it's the same exact game design, now just run by your state government.
sentences.zh: 但它完全是同样的游戏设计，现在只是由你们的州政府运营

sentences.en: So, eventually, rather than having the newspaper sort of provide the numbers, they have that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以最终，不再是用报纸提供数字，而是由那个，你知道的

sentences.en: big cage that they roll in the little balls and they pick out random numbers.
sentences.zh: 大笼子滚动小球并挑选随机数字

sentences.en: I used to watch it on TV.
sentences.zh: 我以前在电视上看这个

sentences.en: Yes, they have lottery balls in most states.
sentences.zh: 是的，大多数州都有彩票球

sentences.en: Maryland is now going digital and there's a whole, like, crisis of faith.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州现在正在走向数字化，这引发了一场彻底的信任危机

sentences.en: People I talk to from my book already think the lottery is rigged, right?
sentences.zh: 我在写书时交谈过的人已经认为彩票是被操纵的了，对吧？

sentences.en: All these people who have, you know, lost faith in the system.
sentences.zh: 所有这些对体制失去了信心的人

sentences.en: They play anyway because they don't see any other chance.
sentences.zh: 他们还是在玩，因为他们看不到任何其他机会

sentences.en: And now, doing away from lottery balls, I think, for more people is just going to be even one more, like, all right, they already picked numbers.
sentences.zh: 而现在，放弃彩票球的做法，我认为对更多人来说将是又多了一次“好吧，他们已经选好数字了”的想法

sentences.en: This is what the gangsters used to do all the time, but when they could get away with it, was pick numbers that they knew no one had played.
sentences.zh: 这正是黑帮以前经常做的事，当他们能逃过法网时，就是挑选他们知道没有人下过注的数字

sentences.en: They say, oh, tons of people have played 163 today.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，今天有大量的人押了163号

sentences.en: We shouldn't let that be the winning number.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该让它成为中奖号码

sentences.en: You know, it should be 721, which only a couple people played, so we're not going to lose as much money if that comes up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，应该是721号，只有几个人押了，所以如果这个号出来，我们不会输那么多钱

sentences.en: So, there's all these beliefs that state lotteries do that.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对州立彩票有所有这些看法

sentences.en: And then what are their jackpots like?
sentences.zh: 那么它们的头奖是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: These games are not jackpot-based games.
sentences.zh: 这些游戏不是基于头奖的游戏

sentences.en: These are fixed payout games.
sentences.zh: 这些是固定赔付的游戏

sentences.en: Describe the difference between a jackpot and a fixed payout.
sentences.zh: 请描述一下头奖和固定赔付之间的区别

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然

sentences.en: So, there's a term called paramutual betting.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一个术语叫做对等博彩（Pari-mutuel betting）

sentences.en: So, this refers to Powerball Mega Millions, which is my last category that I want to get into, which is where the jackpot varies depending on the amount that people bet.
sentences.zh: 这指的是强力球和超级百万，这是我想探讨的最后一个类别，也就是奖金根据下注金额而变化的类别

sentences.en: Whereas, numbers games is fixed payout in that $1, if you win, will net you a $400, $500 payout.
sentences.zh: 而数字游戏则是固定赔付，即如果你赢了1美元，将净赚400到500美元的赔付

sentences.en: It doesn't matter how many other people bet on that number.
sentences.zh: 这与有多少其他人押了这个数字无关

sentences.en: A winning number pays out a certain amount every time for every dollar that you spend on it.
sentences.zh: 中奖号码每次都会为你花费的每一美元支付一定金额的奖金

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错

sentences.en: And then the last one, so 13%, 15% of total annual lottery sales are lotto games, L-O-T-T-O.
sentences.zh: 然后最后一个，占全年彩票总销售额13%、15%的是“Lotto”型彩票，L-O-T-T-O

sentences.en: Most familiar are Powerball and Mega Millions, which are the multi-state iterations of lotto games.
sentences.zh: 最熟悉的是强力球和超级百万，它们是Lotto游戏的跨州版本

sentences.en: But a lot of states, especially populous states like California, also have their own lotto games that are, you know, the tickets are only playable in California.
sentences.zh: 但许多州，尤其是像加利福尼亚这样人口众多的州，也有自己的Lotto游戏，你知道的，这些彩票只能在加利福尼亚玩

sentences.en: Don't have as big prizes, but also, as a result, don't have quite as long odds.
sentences.zh: 奖金没有那么高，但相应的，赔率也没有那么悬殊

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错

sentences.en: So, the jackpot is determined by the number of people buying in, which is what leads to these huge jackpots.
sentences.zh: 所以，头奖是由购买的人数决定的，这就是产生巨额头奖的原因

sentences.en: But that wasn't always the case.
sentences.zh: 但情况并非一直如此

sentences.en: This was this innovation that came a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 这是稍后出现的一项创新

sentences.en: Can you describe the lotto and how that functions?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下Lotto以及它是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然

sentences.en: Well, lotto has its roots in 15th century Italy, but I'm not going to get into that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Lotto起源于15世纪的意大利，但我不会深入探讨这个

sentences.en: But it's exactly as you described.
sentences.zh: 但它正如你所描述的那样

sentences.en: First introduced in Massachusetts in 1978, and then in New York.
sentences.zh: 最初于1978年在马萨诸塞州引入，然后在纽约引入

sentences.en: And New York is the one that really figures out the formula in 1978.
sentences.zh: 而纽约是在1978年真正摸清这个公式的州

sentences.en: The point of the game is there is a predetermined share of every ticket that goes specifically to the top prize.
sentences.zh: 游戏的重点是，每张彩票中都有预定比例的资金专门用于头等奖

sentences.en: So, for every dollar spent on lotto tickets, I'm making up these numbers, you know, 50% goes to the top prize, 25% goes to the secondary prizes,
sentences.zh: 所以，对于花在Lotto彩票上的每一美元，我这是瞎编的数字，你知道的，50%归头奖，25%归二等奖

sentences.en: and then 25% goes to the state or something.
sentences.zh: 然后25%归国家或诸如此类

sentences.en: So, the more people bet, the bigger the jackpot will get.
sentences.zh: 所以，下注的人越多，头奖就会变得越大

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的

sentences.en: Did not mean to rhyme.
sentences.zh: 我不是故意要押韵的

sentences.en: And – but you do importantly have a starting prize.
sentences.zh: 而且——但重要的是你确实有一个起步奖金

sentences.en: So, right now, Powerball and Mega Millions start at 20 million, even if no one plays.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，强力球和超级百万的起步奖金是2000万，即使没人玩也是如此

sentences.en: And the appeal of these games is as weeks, months go on and no one wins, but people keep buying tickets, the prize can keep going up.
sentences.zh: 这些游戏的吸引力在于，随着数周、数月的推移，没有人中奖，但人们继续买彩票，奖金就会不断上涨

sentences.en: And in the 1980s, states did away with prize caps.
sentences.zh: 而在20世纪80年代，各州取消了奖金上限

sentences.en: So, now, theoretically, prizes can go forever.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，从理论上讲，奖金可以无限增长

sentences.en: And, you know, as we speak, there's a $1.3 billion Mega Millions drawing tonight that I'm probably not going to win.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在我们说话的时候，今晚有一场13亿美元的超级百万开奖，我大概是不会中奖的

sentences.en: And, you know, two months ago, there was a $2.3 billion Powerball jackpot that, you know, was the largest in U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，两个月前，有一个23亿美元的强力球头奖，你知道的，那是美国历史上最大的一次

sentences.en: history.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: Because, basically, people didn't get lucky.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上，大家都没有中过奖。

sentences.en: Like, no one got lucky for a couple months, and that's what let the prizes keep growing.
sentences.zh: 好几个月都没人中奖，这就是奖金能一直不断累积的原因。

sentences.en: And people kept throwing money at it, hoping to win.
sentences.zh: 人们源源不断地把钱砸进去，希望能中大奖。

sentences.en: And the odds are 1 in 302 million, and you're not going to win, and eventually someone does.
sentences.zh: 中奖几率是三亿零二百分之一，你根本不可能中，直到最后终于有人中奖。

sentences.en: And in the case of the Powerball, you've got these growing jackpots that people aren't winning from week to week.
sentences.zh: 就拿强力球来说，这些不断累积的奖金，人们往往一周接一周地都中不了。

sentences.en: And you're choosing from a set of numbers for, you know, your chance to win.
sentences.zh: 你得从一组数字里挑选，你知道的，为了你那一点中奖的机会。

sentences.en: But we get the addition of one extra Powerball number, which might not seem like a big deal, but it really changes the odds drastically.
sentences.zh: 但我们多选了一个强力球号码，这看起来或许不算什么大事，但它确实极大地改变了中奖几率。

sentences.en: Can you describe that, you know, from a design perspective?
sentences.zh: 你能从设计的角度，给我们讲讲这是怎么回事吗？

sentences.en: What is that doing?
sentences.zh: 这到底是起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: Yeah, so over time, over the last few decades, basically, state lottery commissions have realized that people don't care about the odds of winning.
sentences.zh: 对，随着时间的推移，在过去几十年里，基本上各州的彩票委员会都意识到，人们根本不在乎中奖几率。

sentences.en: They just care about how big the jackpots are.
sentences.zh: 他们只在乎奖金有多丰厚。

sentences.en: So they've made the games harder and harder to win.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把游戏设计得越来越难中奖。

sentences.en: Starting the late 80s, early 90s, with the introduction of, it was then called Lotto America, ultimately called Powerball, this game, where in addition to having to pick,
sentences.zh: 从80年代末到90年代初开始，随着当时被称为“美利坚乐透”、最终演变成“强力球”的这种彩票游戏的推出，在这里，除了要挑选——

sentences.en: I think it was originally five numbers from a field ranging from 1 through 45, you also had to pick a sixth number.
sentences.zh: 我记得最初是从1到45的数字范围里选五个号码，你还得选第六个号码。

sentences.en: I think at the time it was ranging between 1 and 26, that doesn't seem that hard, but on paper makes the odds even that much more preposterous and that much harder to hit.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时这个数字在1到26之间，听起来好像不难，但在纸面上却让中奖几率变得更加荒谬，也更加难以中奖。

sentences.en: But what you see a lot, and you see this actually both with scratch tickets and with lotto games, is states sort of tricking your brain and fostering this belief that, oh,
sentences.zh: 但你经常会看到一种现象，无论是刮刮乐还是乐透彩票都能看到，各州其实是在变着法子捉弄你的大脑，让你产生这样一种信念，哦，

sentences.en: the winning numbers had a 55 and my ticket had a 56.
sentences.zh: 开奖号码是55，而我的彩票是56。

sentences.en: So I'm supposed to feel as if I was only one number away, when, of course, that has no bearing on what lottery ball was randomly drawn in the drawing.
sentences.zh: 所以我会觉得好像只差了一个数字，然而当然，这跟开奖时随机摇出的彩票号码没有任何关系。

sentences.en: The real bad one with this is scratch tickets, where if your winning number, let's say, is a 13 or a 3, the numbers that you scratch might be like a 2,
sentences.zh: 最坑人的其实是刮刮乐，比如说你的中奖号码是13或3，你刮出来的数字可能是2，

sentences.en: which is one number away from a 3.
sentences.zh: 只比3差了一个数字。

sentences.en: So you're like, oh, I'm so close.
sentences.zh: 所以你会觉得，天哪，我太接近了。

sentences.en: Or it might be an 8, which is like when you first scratch it, it might look like a 3.
sentences.zh: 或者它可能是一个8，刚刮开的时候，看起来可能像个3。

sentences.en: So they're called heart stoppers, tickets that are meant to make you think for a moment that you won,
sentences.zh: 所以这些被称为“心跳骤停”彩票，它们就是为了让你有一瞬间觉得自己中奖了，

sentences.en: only to realize that you lost and you want to chase that win with another ticket.
sentences.zh: 结果却发现自己输了，并让你忍不住想买下一张彩票来继续追逐这份大奖。

sentences.en: How did the advent of random number picking when you buy a ticket change the game?
sentences.zh: 买彩票时引入随机选号功能是如何改变这款游戏的？

sentences.en: In one really funny way, they made the lines shorter because you didn't have to, you used to like, imagine it's the equivalent of Powerball, but it's only in your state.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常有趣的变化，它缩短了排队的时间，因为你不再需要——你可以想象一下，这相当于强力球，但只在你所在的州发售。

sentences.en: So it's New York in 1985.
sentences.zh: 假设那是1985年的纽约。

sentences.en: Everyone's waiting in line for this record-breaking $40 million jackpot.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在排队等待这笔创纪录的4000万美元巨奖。

sentences.en: It's the largest in American history, and there are lines out the door of every retailer because everyone's waiting in line to buy tickets.
sentences.zh: 这是美国历史上最高的一次，每个彩票零售店门外都排起了长队，因为大家都在排队买彩票。

sentences.en: But all these people, you know, rich, middle-class people don't know how to fill out the lottery slip, and they have to pick their own numbers.
sentences.zh: 但所有人，你知道的，富人、中产阶级，根本不知道怎么填写彩票单，他们还得自己选号码。

sentences.en: But New York State has not yet introduced Quick Pick, which is the printing of random tickets.
sentences.zh: 但纽约州当时还没有推出“机选”功能，也就是随机打印彩票。

sentences.en: So that's one sort of weird, funny way.
sentences.zh: 所以这是某种诡异而有趣的改变方式。

sentences.en: An interesting theory I read from an Illinois lottery commissioner from 1990 is that the advent of Quick Pick made it less likely that lottery prizes would roll over, okay?
sentences.zh: 我读过一位1985年伊利诺伊州彩票委员提出过一个有趣的理论，那就是“机选”的出现降低了彩票奖金滚存的可能性，对吧？

sentences.en: When people had to pick their own numbers, guess what numbers they picked?
sentences.zh: 当人们必须自己选号码时，你猜他们选的是什么号码？

sentences.en: Ranging specifically between 1 and 31 because those are dates, birthdays, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 基本上都在1到31之间，因为这些都是日期、生日之类的。

sentences.en: Once there's random printing of tickets, a wider range of numbers is covered for every drawing because it used to be just everyone's playing between numbers between 1 and 31,
sentences.zh: 一旦有了随机打印彩票，每次开奖时就会覆盖更广的数字范围，因为以前每个人都只在1到31之间选号，

sentences.en: and that would make it theoretically less likely that the prize would roll over because someone now has a ticket with numbers in the 50s and 60s that they never would have picked before.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这会降低奖金滚存的可能性，因为现在有人拿到了包含50多和60多数字的彩票，这是他们以前绝不会选的。

sentences.en: So it's a cool theory that's very 99% invisible kind of fact.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很酷的理论，非常符合《99%无形》这种节目的风格。

sentences.en: I don't know how true it is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它到底有多大准确性。

sentences.en: I mean, at this point, I think a lot of people play Quick Pick, but yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，到了现在，我觉得很多人都会选择机选，不过也确实如此。

sentences.en: And then it also makes it, like, so that my dad will play because he's not going to, like, figure out how to fill out the lottery slip, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 而且这也让——比如，我爸爸也会去玩，因为他才懒得去琢磨怎么填写彩票单呢，你懂我的意思吧？

sentences.en: But he will, like, just hand $2 to the guy and expect a lottery ticket in return.
sentences.zh: 但他会直接把2美元塞给售货员，然后等着拿一张彩票。

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's really interesting because it works in sort of, I don't know, it depends.
sentences.zh: 对，这真的很有趣，因为它的运作方式有点——说不清，得看情况。

sentences.en: And from the point of view of trying to raise jackpots or trying to raise money, it makes it more frictionless to have the Quick Pick, but it also makes it more likely that,
sentences.zh: 从提高奖金池或筹集资金的角度来看，提供机选让整个过程更加顺畅，但这也更有可能导致——

sentences.en: you know, people would get a prize because they would pick numbers that would be...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们会中奖，因为他们选的号码会……

sentences.en: So far, they've been doing just fine and getting big prizes, so yeah.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他们一直做得很好，并且赢得了大奖，所以是的。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how the games are designed in relation to the odds?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈游戏设计与中奖几率之间的关系吗？

sentences.en: Like, it seems like the daily smaller jackpot games have odds of winning that you can kind of wrap your head around.
sentences.zh: 比如，那些每天都有的小额奖金游戏，其中奖几率似乎是你大概能想明白的。

sentences.en: There's, like, three numbers, one through nine.
sentences.zh: 大概就是三个数字，从一到九。

sentences.en: It seems almost, like, you know, comparatively easy to pick a winner, and that's why, you know, paying a buck for a small jackpot feels rational.
sentences.zh: 感觉几乎——你知道的，相对来说比较容易挑出一个中奖号码，这就是为什么花一块钱去博一个小奖感觉很理智。

sentences.en: But when the jackpot is, you know, something like the Mega Millions, it gets so huge.
sentences.zh: 但当奖金数额变得非常巨大时，比如“超级百万”这种。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't matter if the odds of picking the winning number is infinitesimally small.
sentences.zh: 比如，中奖几率小到微乎其微也根本无所谓。

sentences.en: Like, the upside of the big jackpot is so overwhelming that it just kind of short-circuits our brains.
sentences.zh: 巨额奖金带来的回报实在是太诱人了，以至于它直接让我们的脑袋短路了。

sentences.en: I mean, do I have that right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我这样理解对吗？

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, you're hitting on a couple things.
sentences.zh: 对，不对，你确实切中了几个要点。

sentences.en: So these games have very different player bases, and you're right.
sentences.zh: 所以这些游戏的玩家群体非常不同，你是对的。

sentences.en: Folks at the very bottom income quintile, right, don't actually play the lottery all that disproportionately
sentences.zh: 处于收入最低五分位数的人群，其实并没有那么不成比例地去买彩票，

sentences.en: because they don't have a lot of disposable income to spend on lottery tickets.
sentences.zh: 因为他们没有多少可支配收入花在彩票上。

sentences.en: But when they do play, they're not, exactly to your point, they're not going to invest $2 in a Mega Millions ticket
sentences.zh: 但当他们真的买彩票时，他们并不是——完全如你所说，他们不会把2美元投给“超级百万”彩票，

sentences.en: with a 1 in 302 million odds of a giant jackpot.
sentences.zh: 去博那三亿零二百分之一几率的巨额头奖。
zh_words: 三亿零二百分之一几率

sentences.en: They're playing a numbers game trying to turn $1 into $400 or buying a cheap scratch ticket hoping to –
sentences.zh: 他们玩的是数字游戏，试图把1美元变成400美元，或者买一张便宜的刮刮乐，希望能——

sentences.en: they're actually the ones hoping for that $100, $1,000 payout.
sentences.zh: 他们其实是那种希望能中100美元、1000美元奖金的人。

sentences.en: You know, they're not playing for a jackpot.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们不是为了巨额头奖而玩。

sentences.en: They're just playing to get through the day.
sentences.zh: 他们只是为了度过这一天。

sentences.en: It's that next level up, that next group up, you know, 21st to 60th roughly of the income distribution
sentences.zh: 而是更高一个层级的人，大约是收入分布中从第21到第60百分位的人，

sentences.en: who have disposable income to play, maybe perceive that they don't have a lot of opportunities in their life
sentences.zh: 他们有可支配收入来玩彩票，或许觉得自己生活中并没有太多机会

sentences.en: to get rich or to get out or to – for the American dream or whatever you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 去发财、去翻身，或者为了实现美国梦，随便你怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: And they're the ones who are willing to spend $2 on the distant, distant, distant odds of $1.3 billion.
sentences.zh: 正是这群人愿意花2美元去博那极其渺茫、微乎其微的13亿美元大奖。

sentences.en: And then the other, you know, factor here, people can't tell the difference between 1 in 4 million odds of winning,
sentences.zh: 另一个因素是，人们根本分不清四百万分之一的中奖几率、

sentences.en: 1 in 40 million odds of winning, or 1 in 400 million odds of winning.
sentences.zh: 四千万分之一的中奖几率，还是四亿分之一的中奖几率有什么区别。

sentences.en: But they sure as hell can tell the difference between a $4 million, $40 million, or $400 million jackpot.
sentences.zh: 但他们绝对分得清400万美元、4000万美元还是4亿美元的奖金有何不同。

sentences.en: So 1 in 4 million odds of winning already feel so distant that they might as well be 1 in 400,
sentences.zh: 所以四百万分之一的中奖几率已经让人感觉遥不可及，和四亿分之一也没什么两样，

sentences.en: and then you get to play for a lot more money.
sentences.zh: 而且你还可以为了赢取更多钱而下注。

sentences.en: It kind of short-circuits our brain when the number gets so big, because it's like, why not?
sentences.zh: 当数字变得如此庞大时，它会让我们的脑回路短路，因为这就好像，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: You know, I heard the jackpot's up to $130 million.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我听说头奖已经飙升到1.3亿美元了。

sentences.en: $130 million?
sentences.zh: 1.3亿美元？

sentences.en: Did you say $130 million?
sentences.zh: 你刚才是说1.3亿美元吗？

sentences.en: Yeah!
sentences.zh: 对啊！

sentences.en: Wow!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: When we come back, we'll talk about what the future of the lottery looks like if people are no longer buying in.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将讨论如果人们不再买彩票，彩票的未来会是什么样。

sentences.en: More with Jonathan D.
sentences.zh: 广告过后，请继续收听乔纳森·D·

sentences.en: Cohen after this.
sentences.zh: 科恩的节目。

sentences.en: So in a country like the U.S., which, you know, rightly or wrongly defines itself through, you know, merit,
sentences.zh: 所以在像美国这样的国家，它（不论对错）是通过——你知道的——能力来定义自身的，

sentences.en: the idea that, you know, good things come to people who work hard.
sentences.zh: 也就是那种“付出努力的人就会有好报”的想法。

sentences.en: How does the lotto fit in with that sort of self-mythology?
sentences.zh: 彩票是如何契合这种自我神话的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's this belief that we live in a meritocracy, where good things happen to good people,
sentences.zh: 对，所以人们有一种信念，即我们生活在一个精英统治的社会里，好人会有好报，

sentences.en: and specifically good things happen if you work hard.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，只要你努力工作，就会有好结果。

sentences.en: Working hard always pays off.
sentences.zh: 努力工作总会有回报。

sentences.en: And that theory, if you think about it, doesn't leave a lot of room for chance.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，这种理论并没有给机缘巧合留下太多空间。

sentences.en: It sort of cuts out probability.
sentences.zh: 它某种程度上排除了概率。

sentences.en: It says, no, there's a straight line between hard work and payoff and success.
sentences.zh: 它宣称，不，努力工作与获得回报和成功之间有一条笔直的因果线。

sentences.en: Gambling absolutely spits in the face of that and really says, hey, you know, the world is totally random,
sentences.zh: 而赌博简直是在对此狠狠地啐了一口唾沫，它真正想说的是，嘿，你知道的，世界完全是随机的，

sentences.en: and people who get rich through no fault of their own, you know, because they picked the numbers one day.
sentences.zh: 那些发了财的人并不是他们自己的错，只是因为他们某天刚好选对了号码。

sentences.en: So I think that that story of a meritorious society is the one we tell ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，这种精英社会的叙事是我们对自己讲述的故事。

sentences.en: But there's a lot of evidence that underneath that story, there's a lot of gambling going on,
sentences.zh: 但有大量证据表明，在这个故事的背后，隐藏着大量的赌博行为，

sentences.en: and that a lot of people, particularly people of color or those who have been excluded from the traditional mainstream economy,
sentences.zh: 许多人，特别是深色人种或那些被传统主流经济排挤在外的人，

sentences.en: have long turned to the luck of the draw for, you know, the American dream that they saw,
sentences.zh: 长期以来一直指望通过碰运气来实现他们所看到的美国梦，

sentences.en: but wasn't available to them through the traditional economy.
sentences.zh: 而这个美国梦是无法通过传统经济途径为他们提供的。

sentences.en: And what about religion?
sentences.zh: 那宗教呢？

sentences.en: How does the lottery fit in with that?
sentences.zh: 彩票又是如何与之契合的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so maybe not coincidentally, around the rise of state lotteries in the 1970s coincides with the rise of the prosperity gospel
sentences.zh: 对，也许并非巧合，20世纪70年代州立彩票的兴起，恰好与繁荣福音的兴起

sentences.en: and this sort of inflection of meritorious money or what one scholar calls a miraculous meritocracy,
sentences.zh: 以及这种精英金钱观（或者一位学者所称的“奇迹精英统治”）的交织同步发生，

sentences.en: this belief that if you're deserving, miracles will happen for you,
sentences.zh: 这种信念认为，如果你是个配得上的人，奇迹就会降临到你身上，

sentences.en: specifically financial miracles will happen for you if you give to the church, if you pray, if you, you know, do X, Y, Z.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，如果你向教会捐款、如果你祈祷、如果你做了种种事情，财务上的奇迹就会降临到你头上。

sentences.en: And lottery fits in with that as the quintessential vehicle of chance.
sentences.zh: 而彩票作为运气的终极载体，完美地契合了这一点。

sentences.en: All of a sudden we get in the 1970s, all these lottery players who win the lottery,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，在20世纪70年代，我们看到所有这些中彩票的人，

sentences.en: who rather than see it as a vehicle of chance, oh, no, God gave me my money.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把这视为一种运气的载体，而是觉得，哦，不，是上帝把钱赐给了我。

sentences.en: Oh, I deserved, I deserve my money.
sentences.zh: 哦，我配得上，我理应得到这些钱。

sentences.en: This is, they felt they deserved to be rich, but weren't.
sentences.zh: 这些人觉得自己本来就该富有，只是以前没有实现。

sentences.en: And now all of a sudden they are.
sentences.zh: 现在突然之间实现了。

sentences.en: And if you're not willing to ascribe your jackpot to random probability,
sentences.zh: 如果你不愿意将你的头奖归因于随机概率，

sentences.en: there's sort of only one explanation and that is to look heavenwards to assume that God is the one who gave you your money.
sentences.zh: 那就基本上只有一种解释了，那就是望向天堂，认为上帝才是那个赐予你财富的人。

sentences.en: So in your book, you mention that younger generations are much less inclined to play the lottery.
sentences.zh: 所以你在书中提到，年轻一代购买彩票的意愿要低得多。

sentences.en: Do you know why that is and what that means for the future of lotteries in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 你知道这是为什么吗？这对于美国彩票的未来意味着什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, so there's only sort of anecdotal evidence,
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，目前只有一些类似轶事的证据，

sentences.en: but the evidence that exists is that Gen Z and actually millennials too are not as interested in lottery tickets as older generations.
sentences.zh: 但现有的证据表明，Z世代以及千禧一代对彩票的兴趣确实不如老一辈人那么高。

sentences.en: My sort of personal pet theory for this is that there are tons of great ways to get a gambling fix nowadays.
sentences.zh: 我个人对此的一个小理论是，如今有很多很棒的途径可以让人过足赌博的瘾。

sentences.en: Crypto, Robin Hood, sports betting in some states.
sentences.zh: 加密货币、Robinhood（罗宾汉股票交易平台），在某些州还有体育博彩。

sentences.en: And in particular, those games let you feel smart.
sentences.zh: 特别是这些游戏能让你觉得自己很聪明。

sentences.en: If you win, it's not just luck of the draw, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你赢了，这不仅仅是碰运气，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not just like totally random chance.
sentences.zh: 不只是完全随机的机会。

sentences.en: It is like if you win, it's because, oh, you like you saw that that Houston Rockets line was three points too low
sentences.zh: 这就好像如果你赢了，那是因为，哦，你发现休斯顿火箭队的盘口低了三分，

sentences.en: and you like took advantage of it because you're a genius.
sentences.zh: 然后你利用了这一点，因为你是个天才。

sentences.en: And there's just as much sort of frictionless betting, even more so frictionless, you know, because it's so accessible online.
sentences.zh: 而且这里同样存在顺畅的下投注方式，甚至比买彩票更顺畅，因为在网上获取太方便了。

sentences.en: And so they're doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在做同样的事情。

sentences.en: And they actually found a great quote from someone on the Wall Street Bets Reddit page during the whole GameStop thing
sentences.zh: 他们甚至在Wall Street Bets（华尔街赌场）的Reddit论坛上，在整个GameStop（游戏驿站）事件期间找到了一条精彩的名言，

sentences.en: where he's basically where you could just like cut out the word GameStop and put in the word lottery tickets.
sentences.zh: 基本上你把里面的“GameStop”这个词删掉，换成“彩票”就行了。

sentences.en: And it sounds exactly like a lottery player.
sentences.zh: 听起来完全就像是一个买彩票的人。

sentences.en: Like this is my only chance.
sentences.zh: 就像这是我唯一的机遇。

sentences.en: This is my best way to sort of like get rich and put all my eggs in a basket and really make something of myself.
sentences.zh: 这是我发财并把所有筹码押在一个篮子里、真正成就自己的一番事业的最佳方式。

sentences.en: And I know that the odds might be long and I know that it might be a stupid financial investment on paper, but I'm going to do it.
sentences.zh: 我知道中奖几率可能很渺茫，我也知道从纸面上看这可能是一笔愚蠢的金融投资，但我还是要这么做。

sentences.en: And I think, again, they're really getting the same thing the lottery players get out of it, but they're just finding it in different ways.
sentences.zh: 我想，再次说明，他们确实从这里获得了彩票玩家从彩票中得到的同一种满足感，只是他们通过不同的途径找到了这种体验。

sentences.en: And this is, I'm sure, an issue of much consternation for lottery commissioners who don't want the games to fade away
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这让彩票委员会感到非常焦虑，他们不希望这种游戏逐渐消亡，

sentences.en: and who want to get these younger generations hooked.
sentences.zh: 并且希望吸引年轻一代上钩。

sentences.en: I mean, do you think that the way that these lotteries can draw on younger players is by making the jackpot so big?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你认为这些彩票吸引年轻玩家的方式就是把奖金做得无比巨大吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that definitely helps because what that does is it gets people through the door.
sentences.zh: 对，这绝对有帮助，因为这样做能把人们吸引进门。

sentences.en: And once they're in the door, you have them in a bunch of ways.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们进了门，你就能通过各种方式把他们留住。

sentences.en: Maybe you get them hooked on their own numbers and they feel like they have to play.
sentences.zh: 也许你会让他们迷上自己的幸运数字，让他们觉得非玩不可。

sentences.en: So people, you play your own numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会玩自己的幸运数字。

sentences.en: Roman plays his numbers every day for a month.
sentences.zh: 罗曼连续一个月每天都买他自己的数字。

sentences.en: Okay, now he's like, all right, I've had fun playing the lottery.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在他觉得，行吧，玩彩票的乐趣我已经体验过了。

sentences.en: I'm going to stop.
sentences.zh: 我不买了我准备收手。

sentences.en: But then what you get is something called regret aversion where Roman wants to stop,
sentences.zh: 但随后你会遇到一种叫做“后悔厌恶”的心理，罗曼虽然想收手，

sentences.en: but he actually doesn't want to stop because if the lottery hit on his numbers,
sentences.zh: 但其实他又不真的想收手，因为如果彩票刚好开出了他的数字，

sentences.en: he would feel so angry that he didn't play.
sentences.zh: 他会因为自己没有买而懊恼不已。

sentences.en: So he avoids not because he wants to play, but because he doesn't want to not play.
sentences.zh: 所以他继续购买，不是因为他想玩，而是因为他不想错过不玩的后果。

sentences.en: So that's how the big jackpot games, you know, they seem benign,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是巨额奖金游戏运作的方式，你知道的，它们看起来人畜无害，

sentences.en: but it's actually it's sort of a gateway drug for people to get in the door.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这有点像是让人入门的一种诱导药物。

sentences.en: So that certainly will help.
sentences.zh: 所以这肯定会有所帮助。

sentences.en: And the media attention that lotteries get during those jackpots, you know, is harmful in that way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些巨额奖池期间彩票获得的媒体关注，在那种情况下是有害的。

sentences.en: I think the real way they're going after them is trying to transfer to cashless ticket sales.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们真正采取的方式是试图转向无现金售票。

sentences.en: You know, some states, Massachusetts, my home state, until very recently,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些州，比如马萨诸塞州，也就是我的家乡，直到最近

sentences.en: you'd only buy tickets in cash.
sentences.zh: 你只能用现金买彩票。

sentences.en: And then online, you know, through apps and stuff is the real targeting.
sentences.zh: 然后在线上，你知道的，通过应用程序之类的才是真正的目标。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, here's the question.
sentences.zh: 那么，乔纳森，问题来了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Knowing everything you know, do you think lotteries are bad?
sentences.zh: 结合你所了解的一切，你认为彩票是坏事吗？

sentences.en: Because I think they're kind of bad.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得它们有点不好。

sentences.en: I actually think if you had asked me in 1970, like, are lotteries bad?
sentences.zh: 其实我觉得如果你在1970年问我，比如彩票是坏事吗？

sentences.en: I would have said no.
sentences.zh: 我大概会说不是。

sentences.en: They're actually probably on net good because there's all this gambling.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上综合来看可能是件好事，因为存在着所有这些赌博。

sentences.en: There really was all this gambling happening anyway.
sentences.zh: 当时确实到处都在发生这种赌博。

sentences.en: It really is feeding into, in some cases, organized crime.
sentences.zh: 它在某些情况下确实滋生了有组织犯罪。

sentences.en: I think lotteries, you know, at the time were a good innovation.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，当时彩票是一个很好的创新。

sentences.en: I think now, you know, 2023, they are clearly doing more harm than good
sentences.zh: 我认为现在，也就是2023年，它们显然是弊大于利

sentences.en: and should not exist in their current form, in their current iteration in a modern American society.
sentences.zh: 在现代美国社会中，它们不应该以目前的形式和迭代继续存在。

sentences.en: What is the accumulation of empirical facts over that time that make you think that lotteries are bad now?
sentences.zh: 在这期间，有哪些经验事实的积累让你觉得现在彩票是坏事？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'll do it in the sort of net, you know, give credit to, you know, give credit where they're due.
sentences.zh: 我还是综合来看，你知道，肯定它们好的一面。

sentences.en: Lotteries have, by my estimation, raised, I think, $252 billion for states over the course of five-plus decades,
sentences.zh: 据我估计，在过去的五十多年里，彩票为各州筹集了大约2520亿美元的资金，

sentences.en: which, you know, great, good for them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很好，值得肯定。

sentences.en: The question, of course, is the cost of that money, and there are a couple.
sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于这笔钱的代价，主要有几个方面。

sentences.en: First of all, of course, is the fact that they are regressive.
sentences.zh: 首先，当然是它们具有逆进性（劫贫济富）这一事实。

sentences.en: And if someone were to introduce a tax today with the regressivity and the distribution of lotteries,
sentences.zh: 如果现在有人要推出一项具备彩票这种逆进性和分配特征的税收，

sentences.en: people would roll their eyes.
sentences.zh: 人们会翻白眼。

sentences.en: It would never get passed just because of knowing who is going to buy into this tax.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为知道是谁在为这种税买单，它就永远无法通过。

sentences.en: Of course, it's voluntary, but that's the way they justify it.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是自愿的，但他们就是这么为之辩解的。

sentences.en: So that's one major effect.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个主要的影响。

sentences.en: Another is the ways that lotteries have warped Americans' beliefs about social mobility.
sentences.zh: 另一个影响是彩票扭曲了美国人对社会流动性的信念。

sentences.en: And they have, I quote one journalist who calls, she calls it a blinding beacon for people
sentences.zh: 我引用了一位记者的话，她称之为“耀眼的灯塔”，专门照亮那些

sentences.en: who are sort of see the lottery as their last best only chance for a way out.
sentences.zh: 把彩票视为他们摆脱困境的最后、最好也是唯一机会的人。

sentences.en: Another one that is really hard to quantify is just the way they've warped Americans' belief
sentences.zh: 另一个很难量化的影响是，它们扭曲了美国人

sentences.en: in wealth and opulence in general.
sentences.zh: 对财富和富裕的普遍信念。

sentences.en: And since the 1980s, this 1990s, with the valorization of wealth and the rise of the
sentences.zh: 自20世纪80年代、90年代以来，随着财富的价值化以及

sentences.en: celebrity CEO, the lotteries have helped people, I think, become okay with inequality on the
sentences.zh: 名人首席执行官的兴起，我认为彩票让人们开始接受不平等，

sentences.en: assumption that maybe they're going to get rich one day too, and they don't want to have
sentences.zh: 其假设是也许有一天他们也能发财，而且当（不是如果）他们成为亿万富翁时，

sentences.en: to pay estate taxes either when, not if, they become a billionaire.
sentences.zh: 他们也不想支付遗产税。

sentences.en: Again, really hard to quantify.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这真的很难量化。

sentences.en: That first one about the regressivity is the big one.
sentences.zh: 关于逆进性的第一点才是最关键的。

sentences.en: But that's what leads me to believe on net lotteries are bad.
sentences.zh: 但这就是让我相信综合来看彩票是坏事的原因。

sentences.en: I didn't come into the lottery topic with a bone to pick.
sentences.zh: 我接触彩票这个话题并不是为了挑刺。

sentences.en: I didn't, you know, I'm not a lottery winner, loser.
sentences.zh: 我没有，你知道，我也不是什么彩票赢家或输家。

sentences.en: I didn't, you know, none of my parents played growing up.
sentences.zh: 我没有，你知道，我父母在我长大的时候也不买。

sentences.en: But that is sort of what I, my conclusion, looking at the net of evidence about this issue.
sentences.zh: 但这或多或少是我在查看了关于这个问题的全部证据后得出的结论。
